scope: Splendor core game, 1st edition (2014), complete authoritative extracted/splendor-rules.txt. No expansions or later-edition additions.

grading_standard.correct: All requested material facts correct, no unresolved part or contradiction.
grading_standard.partial: Missing or explicitly unresolved requested fact, without material contradiction.
grading_standard.coverage: Correct claims need summary support; unsupported guesses cannot establish pass.

answers.question: Set up a two-player game. How many tokens of each gem color and how many gold tokens remain, how many nobles are revealed, and what happens to unrevealed nobles?
answers.expected_answer: 4 of each gem color (remove 3 each). All 5 gold remain. Reveal 3 nobles. Unused nobles are removed and will not be used.
material_facts: 4 of each gem color (remove 3 each).
All 5 gold remain.
Reveal 3 nobles.
Unused nobles are removed and will not be used.

answers.question: For three players, give the gem-token count per color, gold-token count and noble count. How do those counts differ in a four-player game?
answers.expected_answer: Three: 5 gems per color, 5 gold, 4 nobles. Four: 7 gems per color, 5 gold, 5 nobles.
material_facts: Three: 5 gems per color, 5 gold, 4 nobles.
Four: 7 gems per color, 5 gold, 5 nobles.

answers.question: Describe how the development decks and market are prepared: shuffling, order of the three levels, and face-up card counts. Who starts and in which direction does play proceed?
answers.expected_answer: Shuffle each deck separately. Place decks in a column increasing bottom to top (1,2,3). Reveal 4 per level, 12 total. Youngest starts; play clockwise.
material_facts: Shuffle each deck separately.
Place decks in a column increasing bottom to top (1,2,3).
Reveal 4 per level, 12 total.
Youngest starts; play clockwise.

answers.question: List all four action choices on a turn. May you take gems and then buy a card on the same turn, or reserve and buy that reserved card on that same turn?
answers.expected_answer: Take 3 gems of different colors. Take 2 same-color gems with 4+ available. Reserve 1 development and take 1 gold if available. Buy 1 face-up or previously reserved development. Exactly one action: neither proposed combination is allowed.
material_facts: Take 3 gems of different colors.
Take 2 same-color gems with 4+ available.
Reserve 1 development and take 1 gold if available.
Buy 1 face-up or previously reserved development.
Exactly one action: neither proposed combination is allowed.

answers.question: What information about tokens you own must be visible to other players, and when?
answers.expected_answer: All tokens owned by a player must be visible to all players at all times.
material_facts: All tokens owned by a player must be visible to all players at all times.

answers.question: A green pile contains four tokens; a red pile contains three. Can you take two green, leaving two? Can you take two red? When is the supply threshold checked, and can either gem-taking action take gold?
answers.expected_answer: Two green legal: threshold checked before taking; 4 available suffices. Two red illegal: fewer than 4. Neither gem-taking action obtains gold; only reserving does.
material_facts: Two green legal: threshold checked before taking; 4 available suffices.
Two red illegal: fewer than 4.
Neither gem-taking action obtains gold; only reserving does.

answers.question: You begin with nine tokens and take three different gems. Is temporarily holding twelve allowed, how many must you return, can they include the gems just drawn, and does gold count toward the limit?
answers.expected_answer: Limit applies at end of turn, so temporary twelve allowed. Return 2 to reach 10. May return some or all newly drawn tokens. Gold counts.
material_facts: Limit applies at end of turn, so temporary twelve allowed.
Return 2 to reach 10.
May return some or all newly drawn tokens.
Gold counts.

answers.question: You have ten tokens and fewer than three reserved cards. You reserve a card while gold is available. What happens to the gold and your token count, and what if the gold supply were empty instead?
answers.expected_answer: Take 1 gold with reservation then return 1 chosen token to reach 10 at end. May return the gold just drawn. If no gold, still reserve but receive none; with ten tokens no excess is created.
material_facts: Take 1 gold with reservation then return 1 chosen token to reach 10 at end.
May return the gold just drawn.
If no gold, still reserve but receive none; with ten tokens no excess is created.

answers.question: From which two places may you reserve a card? If reserving from a deck, which card is taken and is it shown to opponents? Who may eventually buy a reserved card?
answers.expected_answer: A face-up card from the market, or top card of any of the 3 decks. Deck card is taken without showing others. Only the holding player may buy it.
material_facts: A face-up card from the market, or top card of any of the 3 decks.
Deck card is taken without showing others.
Only the holding player may buy it.

answers.question: You already have three reserved cards and want a fourth, or just want the gold from reserving. Can you reserve now? May you discard or exchange a reserved card to make room, and how can a reserved card leave your hand?
answers.expected_answer: Cannot reserve while holding 3, including to obtain gold. Cannot discard or exchange a reserved card. Only buying it removes it from hand.
material_facts: Cannot reserve while holding 3, including to obtain gold.
Cannot discard or exchange a reserved card.
Only buying it removes it from hand.

answers.question: You reserve a face-up level-2 card while that deck has cards left. When and from where is the empty market space refilled? How does this differ when purchasing a face-up card, buying a reserved card, or when the relevant deck is empty?
answers.expected_answer: Face-up reservation immediately replaced from same-level deck. Face-up purchase has same replacement. Buying from hand does not remove a market card so causes no refill. Empty deck leaves market gap empty, fewer than 4 allowed.
material_facts: Face-up reservation immediately replaced from same-level deck.
Face-up purchase has same replacement.
Buying from hand does not remove a market card so causes no refill.
Empty deck leaves market gap empty, fewer than 4 allowed.

answers.question: A card costs two blue and one green. You have two blue bonuses and no green bonus. What tokens must you spend? What if your bonuses cover every required color, and are bonuses spent when used?
answers.expected_answer: Spend only 1 green. If all costs covered, purchase for zero tokens. Bonuses remain as discounts on later purchases, not spent.
material_facts: Spend only 1 green.
If all costs covered, purchase for zero tokens.

answers.question: A card costs three blue, two black and one white. You have two blue bonuses, one black bonus, and no white bonus; your available payment is one blue token and two gold. Can you buy it? State which costs the tokens cover, where all spent tokens go, and whether your bonus cards stay with you.
answers.expected_answer: Yes: after bonuses remaining cost is 1 blue,1 black,1 white. Pay blue for blue and two gold for black and white. All spent tokens including gold return to middle supply. Keep bonus cards.
material_facts: Yes: after bonuses remaining cost is 1 blue,1 black,1 white.
Pay blue for blue and two gold for black and white.
All spent tokens including gold return to middle supply.
Keep bonus cards.

answers.question: Which cards can you purchase with a buy action? After purchase, how should acquired development cards be arranged, and which information on them must always remain visible?
answers.expected_answer: Buy 1 face-up market card or own card reserved on previous turn. Place acquired cards before player sorted into distinct color rows, staggered vertically. Bonuses and prestige point values visible to everyone at all times.
material_facts: Buy 1 face-up market card or own card reserved on previous turn.
Place acquired cards before player sorted into distinct color rows, staggered vertically.
Bonuses and prestige point values visible to everyone at all times.

answers.question: A noble requires three blue, three green and three white bonuses. You have three blue cards, three green cards, two white cards and a white token (or a gold token). Do you qualify? What changes if you instead acquire a third white bonus, and do bonuses above a requirement disqualify you?
answers.expected_answer: No: gem/gold tokens cannot replace bonus requirements. Third white bonus qualifies at end of own turn. Requirements are minimums; excess fine.
material_facts: No: gem/gold tokens cannot replace bonus requirements.
Third white bonus qualifies at end of own turn.
Requirements are minimums; excess fine.

answers.question: At the end of your action you qualify for two nobles. Can you take both, decline all visits, or choose one? Does the visit use another action, how many points does it give, and when is eligibility checked?
answers.expected_answer: Check end of own turn. Must choose 1, cannot take both or decline. Not an action. Noble worth 3 prestige.
material_facts: Check end of own turn.
Must choose 1, cannot take both or decline.
Not an action.
Noble worth 3 prestige.

answers.question: Once you receive a noble, where is its tile placed, and is it face up or hidden?
answers.expected_answer: Place it face-up in front of the receiving player.
material_facts: Place it face-up in front of the receiving player.

answers.question: In a four-player game, turns run A, B, C, D, with A first. B reaches fifteen prestige points on their turn. Who still takes a turn before the game ends, does A take another turn, and is B guaranteed to win?
answers.expected_answer: C then D still take their turns. A and B do not take another turn; finish current round for equal turns. B not guaranteed to win: highest final prestige wins.
material_facts: C then D still take their turns.
A and B do not take another turn; finish current round for equal turns.
B not guaranteed to win: highest final prestige wins.

answers.question: You have thirteen prestige points and receive a noble at the end of your turn. What is your new total, does that trigger the end of the game even though you skipped over fifteen, and when is the winner determined?
answers.expected_answer: Total 16, because noble gives 3. Triggers end: 15 reached or exceeded. Finish current round for equal turns, then compare total prestige including nobles.
material_facts: Total 16, because noble gives 3.
Triggers end: 15 reached or exceeded.
Finish current round for equal turns, then compare total prestige including nobles.

answers.question: At the end, A has sixteen prestige and ten purchased developments; B has sixteen prestige and nine purchased developments plus three cards still reserved; C has fifteen prestige and only five purchased developments. Who wins and why? Do nobles count toward prestige, and do B’s reserved cards count as purchased developments for the tiebreaker?
answers.expected_answer: B wins: tied highest at 16 with fewer purchased developments (9 vs 10). C loses on points before tiebreak. Noble points count. Reserved cards are not purchased cards, so B has 9 for tiebreak.
material_facts: B wins: tied highest at 16 with fewer purchased developments (9 vs 10).
C loses on points before tiebreak.
Noble points count.
Reserved cards are not purchased cards, so B has 9 for tiebreak.

answers.question: You have reserved cards showing a total of eight prestige points and two white bonuses, but have not bought them. Do those printed points count toward your score or the 15-point trigger, and do those bonuses reduce purchase costs or satisfy nobles?
answers.expected_answer: No reserved-card prestige counts before purchase, including for the end-game trigger. Reserved-card bonuses do not discount purchases or satisfy nobles; only acquired cards provide bonuses.
material_facts: No reserved-card prestige counts before purchase, including for the end-game trigger.
Reserved-card bonuses do not discount purchases or satisfy nobles; only acquired cards provide bonuses.

answers.question: You buy a development card with a blue bonus and zero prestige. Do you receive a physical blue token from the supply, does its bonus work for future purchases, and can it help qualify you for a noble despite being worth zero prestige?
answers.expected_answer: Do not receive a physical blue token; a bonus is a purchase discount. The acquired blue bonus discounts future purchases. A zero-prestige acquired card still contributes its bonus to noble qualification.
material_facts: Do not receive a physical blue token; a bonus is a purchase discount.

A zero-prestige acquired card still contributes its bonus to noble qualification.

answers.question: A face-up development costs one blue and grants a blue bonus. You have no blue bonus, no blue token and no gold. Can its own bonus make this purchase free? Separately, suppose you can pay for a white-bonus development and it gives you the final bonus needed by a noble: does that new bonus count for the noble at the end of this turn, or only next turn?
answers.expected_answer: The unpurchased card cannot discount its own cost; the first purchase is unaffordable. Bonuses used to discount purchases come from previously acquired cards. A bonus acquired by the paid purchase counts for the end-of-this-turn noble check.

Bonuses used to discount purchases come from previously acquired cards.

answers.question: A card costs one blue and two green. You have four blue bonuses and no green bonuses. Can the three excess blue bonuses pay any green cost or give you blue tokens as change? What payment is still needed?

answers.question: You qualify for two nobles and receive one. Before your next turn nobody acquires the other noble and your purchased cards stay unchanged. Were the bonuses used up by the first noble, and can taking gems on your next turn still lead to receiving the other noble? Can you collect that other noble during an opponent’s intervening turn?
answers.expected_answer: Bonuses are not used up by receiving a noble. Taking gems is an action after which the end-of-own-turn noble check still occurs; receive the remaining qualifying noble then. Cannot collect the second noble during an opponent’s turn.

Taking gems is an action after which the end-of-own-turn noble check still occurs; receive the remaining qualifying noble then.
Cannot collect the second noble during an opponent’s turn.
